$comment: Provenance manifest for clinicfinder.co.za data. Declares, per VALUE CLASS, where each value came from. Modelled on SDMX observation-status flags (Eurostat/IMF/FAO).

levels.sourced: Taken from a named third-party open-data source.
levels.derived: Computed from other values in this dataset.
levels.ai_authored: Explanatory prose written by AI over sourced material.
levels.observed: Directly measured by our own tooling at a point in time.
levels.config: Site configuration or build artefact authored by our own tooling — sitemap priorities, routing. Not a factual claim about the world.
levels.not_collected: Field exists in the record shape but was never populated from any source. An honest empty, not a missing value we could fill.
levels.mixed: This field's values do not all share one basis — part sourced, part corrected or computed by us. The split, and the reason for it, is in the notes below.

primary_sources: OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API (1,058 facilities) — community-maintained open data, ODbL licensed.
Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team / HOTOSM exports (18 facilities).
notes: Facility records are SOURCED from open data, not modelled — do not hedge them as estimates. The honest caveat here is different: OpenStreetMap is community-maintained, so completeness and currency vary by area. That is a coverage caveat, not a provenance one, and data_quality_score plus last_verified exist to expose it.
This is a humanitarian site. A wrong clinic address costs someone a trip they may not be able to afford, so the coverage caveat matters more here than anywhere else in the portfolio.

2026-08-14 21:10 SAST — `province` was wrong on 130 of 1,076 facility records (12%), always naming a NEIGHBOURING province. Found by point-in-polygon testing each record's own sourced `coordinates` against the 52 SA district-municipality boundaries (click_that_hood south-africa.geojson) mapped to their provinces. The 130 sit a median 26 km inside the province their coordinates fall in, so this is not boundary noise: Kimberley Hospital was filed under Free State, Ermelo Hospital under KwaZulu-Natal, Sebokeng Hospital under North West, Beaufort West Hospital under Northern Cape. For those records `province` is now DERIVED from `coordinates`, which remain sourced and untouched; the sourced value is not otherwise edited anywhere. 8 of the 130 sit within 3 km of the old province's border and were each confirmed against the town named in their own `address.city` before being changed.

2026-08-19 — `operator_type` was "public" on 16 retail pharmacies (Clicks x3, Dis-Chem x2, Medicross, The Local Choice x2, and 8 independent chemists), all of which also carry the OSM shape label type="clinic". Those two values together rendered the public-primary-care editorial block, which tells the reader a clinic is the front door of the public health system, nurse-driven and free. For those 16 `operator_type` is now DERIVED from the operator identity in `name` (a named national retail pharmacy chain or a private retail chemist is not a public facility); `name`, `type` and every other sourced value are untouched. `type` is left as sourced because it is an honest record of what OSM tags the site as; the reader-facing gate now reads `operator_type`, not `type`.

2026-08-19 — `district` and `sub_district` were EMPTY STRINGS on all 1,076 records while this manifest declared `district` as `sourced`. The OSM/HOTOSM extracts carry no district-municipality tag, so nothing was ever sourced into either field; the declaration was a claim about data that did not exist. `district` is now DERIVED for the 1,067 records whose sourced `coordinates` fall inside an SA district-municipality boundary, by the same point-in-polygon pass that corrected `province` on 2026-08-14 (ops/validate-province-by-coords.py, boundaries from click_that_hood south-africa.geojson, 52 districts). District names are written VERBATIM from that boundary set and are not modernised — a few carry pre-2016/2019 municipal names (Sisonke, uThungulu, Eden) and renaming them by hand would be an unsourced edit. The 9 records that fall outside every SA district boundary keep an empty `district`: siga-home-based-care-north-west, siga-clinic-north-west, bokspits-clinic-northern-cape, domiciliary-clinic-free-state, queen-ii-training-and-domitory-free-state, premier-services-medical-aid-society-limpopo, mafumahali-hospital-maseru, centro-de-saude-de-catuane-kwazulu-natal, centro-de-saude-de-ressano-garcia-mpumalanga (the last three sit in Lesotho and Mozambique). No district name was guessed for them. `sub_district` is not derivable from coordinates at this resolution and is not present upstream, so it is declared `not_collected` rather than left under a false `sourced`; it renders nowhere and no value has been invented for it.

2026-08-19 — `operating_hours.is_24_hour` was TRUE on 449 records whose own `operating_hours.raw` is EMPTY, i.e. asserted with nothing behind it while this manifest declared the whole field `sourced`. The 449 are 419 district hospitals, 7 regional, 1 tertiary and 22 community health centres — the shape of a blanket "a hospital is open 24 hours" rule, not of a source. The dataset refutes that rule where it can be tested: of the 70 hospitals that DO carry sourced hours, 22 (31%) publish times that are not 24-hour (Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00 and similar), and of the 8 CHCs with sourced hours 5 are not 24-hour. The claim was rendered, not dormant: a `24 hours` chip on each facility page, a `24/7` openingHoursSpecification in that page's schema.org LocalBusiness block, a `· 24h` flag in every province listing, the search index, and hub sentences reading "Of these, 516 operate 24 hours" in all three languages. On a humanitarian site that claim sends someone to a closed gate at night. `is_24_hour` is now DERIVED from `raw` and true on the 67 records whose sourced hours say so (63 tagged `24/7` plus 4 spelling out a full day); the other 449 are false, which renders NOTHING rather than a negative claim — absence of published hours is not evidence a facility is closed. No `raw` value was edited. Hub and guide copy in en/xh/zu now reads "recorded as open 24 hours" rather than "operate 24 hours", because what we can vouch for is the record, not the gate. Deriving the 449 back from facility type would need a source we do not have (DoH norms are a legal requirement, not a per-facility observation) and the 22 counter-examples show the rule failing in our own data.

2026-08-19 — vocabulary repair. Three fields (`province`, `operator_type`, `operating_hours`) carried freeform prose in place of a level, e.g. "sourced, with 130 records corrected to derived". That is readable but it broke the two gates that police this file — `tests/provenance-manifest.test.ts` D (every value must be a DEFINED level) and `tests/ai-transparency-page.test.ts` (every level in use must be orderable on /how-this-site-is-made, or it vanishes from the public page silently). Both were RED, and a red gate is one nobody reads. Those three are now the defined level `mixed`, with the split kept where it belongs — in these notes. `not_collected` was also in use (`sub_district`) but absent from the page's LEVEL_ORDER, so it was being dropped from the published provenance key; it is now listed.

2026-08-19 21:20 SAST — `services.emergency_24h` was TRUE on 17 records whose own OpenStreetMap element carries an explicit `emergency=no` tag, i.e. the site asserted the OPPOSITE of what the source says while this manifest declared the whole `services` field `sourced`. Checked by re-querying the Overpass API for the `emergency` tag on all 517 published records claiming emergency_24h. The 17 are not edge cases: they include Panorama Animal Clinic (a VETERINARY practice), "Old Welkom Provincial ( Not in Use)" (decommissioned), Mothibistad Shophhing Centre (a shopping centre), a Clicks pharmacy, an eye clinic and three psychiatric hospitals — every one of them rendering "24-hour emergency" in its <title> meta description, its MedicalClinic schema and its on-page service chips, next to editorial telling the reader to "go directly to the casualty department — no referral needed". Same defect shape as the `operating_hours.is_24_hour` note above: a blanket "a hospital has casualty" rule overriding the source. All 17 are now FALSE, matching their source. No other value was touched and no URL changed, so the field is `mixed` — sourced everywhere except these 17 corrections. NOT fixed and still open: a further 227 published records claim emergency_24h with NO `emergency` tag in OSM at all. Those are unsupported rather than contradicted, and flipping them would strip the emergency listing from roughly half the hospitals on a site whose purpose is directing people to emergency care — the opposite harm. That needs a human decision, not a keeper's.

2026-08-19 22:10 SAST (#1002) — `operator_type` was "unknown" on the 18 records that carry NO service flag at all, and 16 of them are not public facilities. The combination mattered because the reader-facing gate is `operator_type`: with it "unknown" the facility page renders the public-primary-care editorial in all three languages — "a clinic is the front door of the South African public health system", nurse-driven and free — and the schema.org block asserts `isAccessibleForFree: true`. That was rendering on the Salt River state mortuary, on Netcare's Medicross Pretoria West, on a laser/aesthetic clinic (Dermaplastic, Klerksdorp), on an Icon Oncology radiation unit and on a bedding retailer. Each of the 18 was adjudicated INDIVIDUALLY against a second source, never in bulk: 16 are now DERIVED `private` (own website or corporate listing — ihasa.co.za, kpmed.co.za, netcare.co.za, healthemporiummidrand.com, health-worx.co.za, iconsa.co.za, dermaplastic.co.za, medpages listings for The Local Choice Plett and Betesda Gesondheidhuis, dnatest.co.za collection points, dima-health.com for Mogwadi, a Klerksdorp orthopaedic/orthotic practice, a Lenasia chiropractic practice, the Netcare Milpark COVID-19 vaccination site, and vaalio.co.za for Mattress Medi Centre), and 2 are DERIVED `public` — Bafokeng Health Centre, Phokeng (Royal Bafokeng Nation free services, medpages) and Salt River Mortuary (Western Cape Government Forensic Pathology Service, westerncape.gov.za). Three were left `unknown` because no second source could be found: vutlhari-limpopo, sick-bay-kwazulu-natal, nwz-health-centre-gauteng — an unevidenced guess is the thing this manifest exists to prevent. No record was deleted and no sourced value was edited: `name`, `type`, `coordinates` and the empty `services` are untouched, and every URL still resolves. The empty `services` are an ABSENCE in OpenStreetMap, not a claim that these places offer nothing — re-queried via Overpass on 2026-08-19, all 18 objects still exist and all 18 still carry a healthcare tag, so this is missing source data, a different defect from being the wrong kind of place.

2026-08-19 22:40 SAST (#1002) — `care-role.ts` is a new, deliberately tiny registry of published records that are NOT places anyone can be treated: the Salt River state mortuary, an office building in Sandton (Grayston Mews) and a bedding retailer (Mattress Medi Centre). All three are tagged `healthcare` in OpenStreetMap, so no amount of re-querying the source separates them from a clinic — only adjudication against a second source does. That judgement is OURS, so it lives in code beside facility-quality.mjs and is declared `ai_authored`, NOT in facilities.json, which holds sourced values only. Every entry carries the source that settled it. The pages stay live, keep their URLs and stay in the sitemap; what changed is that they no longer render the public-clinic editorial, no longer claim `MedicalClinic` or `isAccessibleForFree` in schema.org, and now say plainly what the place is.
